# spdlog

[gabime/spdlog](https://github.com/gabime/spdlog) · OSS-Fuzz: [projects/spdlog](https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/bd2ce21991a94a362b92fb1bf25f86d5a1a60842/projects/spdlog)

**Status: available.** 5 of OSS-Fuzz's 5 fuzz targets have statements. 20 binaries, 29 MB. 65 statements: 0 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 35 blocked by the model, 30 open.

Built from spdlog (commit `f5f173a1`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [backtrace_fuzzer](backtrace_fuzzer/) | enable_backtrace(n) for a fuzzed uint16 n, then n spdlog::debug calls with fuzzed strings, then dump_backtrace to a /dev/null file sink; output goes to a basic_file_sink on /dev/null and is never read; fmt format errors are caught by spdlog's internal error handler. | none | 13, 7 blocked by the model |
| [format_fuzzer](format_fuzzer/) | pattern_formatter with a custom flag formatter and a fuzzed pattern, then spdlog::info with a fuzzed runtime format string and three arguments; output goes to a basic_file_sink on /dev/null and is never read; fmt format errors are caught by spdlog's internal error handler. | none | 13, 7 blocked by the model |
| [levels_fuzzer](levels_fuzzer/) | cfg::load_env_levels + cfg::load_argv_levels over up to 255 fuzzed argv strings, then spdlog::info; output goes to a basic_file_sink on /dev/null and is never read; fmt format errors are caught by spdlog's internal error handler. | none | 13, 7 blocked by the model |
| [log_fuzzer](log_fuzzer/) | fuzzed runtime format string logged at all six levels via functions and SPDLOG_* macros; output goes to a basic_file_sink on /dev/null and is never read; fmt format errors are caught by spdlog's internal error handler. | none | 13, 7 blocked by the model |
| [pattern_fuzzer](pattern_fuzzer/) | spdlog::set_pattern(whole input); output goes to a basic_file_sink on /dev/null and is never read; fmt format errors are caught by spdlog's internal error handler. | none | 13, 7 blocked by the model |

Not included: **api-driver** (held from this release).

## What the statements say, for spdlog
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.
- **`<build>_disagrees_at_most b`**: for inputs drawn from the harness's `Distribution.v`, the plain and sanitizer builds disagree with probability at most *b*.
- **`<build>_agreement_decidable`**: some riscv64 program decides exactly the finite inputs on which the two builds agree. A program that does so, with a bound on how often it rejects, is a route to a disagreement bound (docs/statements.md).

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch spdlog
    ./oft verify-sha spdlog

By hand: download `spdlog-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.10.0](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0), unpack it into `projects/spdlog/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; an OSS-Fuzz testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [gabime/spdlog](https://github.com/gabime/spdlog) at `f5f173a1a57d0e2e0115f2ed71ee7ea316516853`, built with CMake
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. A binary whose SHA-256 differs after a rebuild with it is a bug: please open an issue.

## Licence
spdlog is under `MIT`. Each binary is a combined work of spdlog, the harness, the C library, the compiler's runtime and every library it links; the SPDX expression of each is not recorded here yet. Corresponding source, in release [v2026.10.0-src](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0-src): `spdlog-src.tar.zst`, the upstream source trees exactly as upstream publishes them; `spdlog-src.MANIFEST.tsv`, which says where the build lays each one down; and `recipe.tar.zst`, that release's build recipe (the build scripts, pins and patches).
